title: Trying to generate embeddings using in-built
body:
## Description

Trying some experiments (Round 1):
1. Started with a "fresh" server (clone of an existing production)
2. Upgraded TS to 0.25
3. Target is a collection with around 18K docs (post, articles etc)
4. Did an update collection to generate embeddings with `ts/all-MiniLM-L12-v2`
5. Server has been churning away since then for 18 hours
6. API calls to this collection dont complete (as expected) while calls to other collections do complete, also as expected
7. Which means that TS is working fine, and its not crashed
8. Next I did a restart on typesense-server.service, however server is still churning away and # 4 is still the behavior

So, this begs some questions:
1. While obviously embeddings are computationally intensive, could they be going for such a long duration?
2. How does one see whats going on, the log doesnt show anything re embeddings AFAICS
3. Shouldnt a service restart stop this. (Of course that might leave the DB is an inconsistent state, so I understand why the activity is resumed post restart)
4. How does one then stop embeddings generation?

## Metadata

**Typesense Version**:
0.25.2

**OS**:
Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS

Yup, I'll do these steps:

Delete all the collections except the relevant one
Target is a collection with around 18K docs (post, articles etc)

At which point you could load and run the alter command.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I'd also like to point out some strange server happenings:

As part of my trials, I selected 2 servers running Typesense - one in the US and another in India.
In both I created a new collection `content1`, with auto embedding (ts/all-MiniLM-L12-v2)
I indexed thousands of the same docs Ive been working with in this set of trials, into `content1`.

Here's the 1st graphic showing server CPU util for the past 1 month in both geos. Until I started with the semantic search trials, the utilization barely went above 20%, and this is most normal.

![image](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/assets/8095144/61b7dcd4-3cd4-4009-ad55-0333ca617684)




The 2nd graphic below shows peaks where I indexed the documents, indexing was done in parallel to both servers. Indexing completed at 0130 on 27/01/24. NO further indexing occurred on `content1` after that.

![image](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/assets/8095144/e0877a00-662a-45e3-acb9-dfb28c769491)



Post that suddenly around 0545 on 27/01/24 the server CPU util shot up to 100%, on BOTH servers, simultaneously. Something that has never occurred before. So what caused this spike, soon after upgrade to 0.25 and auto-embedding generation? It can't be traffic to 2 separate geos simultaneously, and in any case traffic never caused this kind of spike.

Further, both servers became complete unresponsive - no API responses, couldnt SSH etc. Again something that has never ever occurred before.

After this, I rebooted both servers, deleted `content1` from both, and both servers have been humming along like before.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I think this is possibly solved. Previously after looking thru all the logs, it looked like an out-of-memory issue. 

Today Ive tried with:

1. Much better server class
2. TS 26.0
3. 20K docs
4. gte-small

And it got done in about 35 mins (1st spike).

![image](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/assets/8095144/1bfe5803-1a7a-4ef9-baf7-02c1946cc71f)
